The Universe Has No Now, Book 2: Getting There Anyway. Time, Origins, and Whether We Can Get Somewhere Else
It is a complete book. The crew that can wait, and the library that crew would carry, are taught here. You are not sent to another volume to finish this argument.

It comes in two books. This is Book 2, Getting There Anyway: Parts VI to X. The crew that can wait, and the library that crew would carry, are taught here. Book 1, No Now, No Centre, carries Parts I to V; the Previously page before Part VI gives you what this book borrows from it.

paras.text: Book 2: Getting There Anyway
Previously, in Book 1

Book 1, No Now, No Centre, ran from a kitchen to a black hole. Part I took away the universal now: two people in one room slice events differently, light is always late, and what is left is a block of events with your life as one path through it. Part II rebuilt the past we can check: an expansion that happened everywhere at once, a baby picture in microwaves, and the first three minutes.

Part III added a burst, inflation, with its quantum seeds and its untested bubbles. Part IV counted the missing most: the extra pull of dark matter and the shove of dark energy, and why neither hands anyone a forever-mind. Part V met one-way membranes: horizons are facts about events, black holes are not doors, and nothing in this universe hands you a shortcut.

One habit carries over. Every claim wears a temperature: hot for measured, warm for working theory, cold for allowed but not selected by data. This book keeps the same map, the same Notes and Sources, and the same refusal to call a membrane a door. Part VI starts where Book 1 stopped: since you cannot cut through, can you get somewhere anyway?
ALSO BY LOTHAR J. MUSIOL
